_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-steamcmd palworld/egg-palworld.yaml (pelican-eggs, MIT licence), converted to JSON. Console input goes through the egg's own in-container RCON client, as upstream (the RCON port stays inside the container). Octail adds the palworld tag, generic UDP idle sleep (off until staff enable it per server), install sandbox defaults and resource hints. SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". Octail also turns on Palworld's REST API (a published `REST_API_PORT`, written into `OptionSettings` before every start the same way the parser tool writes the other settings there) so the Players tab can list, kick, ban and unban over it; the API is LAN-only, so only Tentacle calls it, never the browser. The config parser is pinned to a release (PARSER_VERSION, v1.0.24) and checked against its SHA-256 (PARSER_SHA256 for another release) instead of the latest release unchecked; a missing server binary or parser fails the install, and a reinstall keeps PalWorldSettings.ini instead of replacing it with the defaults. Broadcasts (restart warnings, schedules) go through the console as `Broadcast` with underscores for spaces. SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Palworld
author: admin@ballaual.de
description:
Fight, farm, build and work alongside mysterious creatures called "Pals" in this completely new
multiplayer, open world survival and crafting game!

startup_commands.Default: CFG="Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini"; if [ -f "$CFG" ]; then if grep -q 'RESTAPIEnabled=' "$CFG"; then sed -i -E "s/RESTAPIEnabled=(True|False)/RESTAPIEnabled=True/; s/RESTAPIPort=[0-9]+/RESTAPIPort=${REST_API_PORT}/" "$CFG"; else sed -i -E "s/OptionSettings=\(/OptionSettings=(RESTAPIEnabled=True,RESTAPIPort=${REST_API_PORT},/" "$CFG"; fi; fi; ./PalworldServerConfigParser; (while read cmd; do rcon -s -a "localhost:$RCON_PORT" -p "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$cmd";done) < /dev/stdin & /home/container/Pal/Binaries/Linux/PalServer-Linux-Shipping Pal -publiclobby -useperfthreads -NoAsyncLoadingThread -UseMultithreadForDS -port={{SERVER_PORT}} -publicport={{SERVER_PORT}} -servername="{{SERVER_NAME}}" -players={{MAX_PLAYERS}} $(if [ -n "$SERVER_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "-serverpassword=\"${SERVER_PASSWORD}\""; fi) -adminpassword="{{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}" -rcon

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# steamcmd Base Installation Script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Based on games-steamcmd's Palworld egg (pelican-eggs, MIT licence). Octail: SteamCMD retried, the config parser
# pinned to a release and checked against its SHA-256, a missing server or parser fails the install, and a reinstall
# keeps PalWorldSettings.ini.

## just in case someone removed the defaults.
if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
    echo -e "steam user is not set.\n"
    echo -e "Using anonymous user.\n"
    STEAM_USER=anonymous
    STEAM_PASS=""
    STEAM_AUTH=""
else
    echo -e "user set to ${STEAM_USER}"
fi

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz || { echo "The SteamCMD download failed."; exit 1; }
tar -xzf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAID} ]] || printf %s "-beta ${SRCDS_BETAID}" ) $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAPASS} ]] || printf %s "-betapassword ${SRCDS_BETAPASS}" ) ${INSTALL_FLAGS} validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f /mnt/server/Pal/Binaries/Linux/PalServer-Linux-Shipping ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Palworld dedicated server. Check the lines above, then reinstall."
    exit 1
fi

## the server's config: created from the shipped defaults when there is none; a reinstall keeps yours
CFG_DIR=/mnt/server/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer
if [ -f "${CFG_DIR}/PalWorldSettings.ini" ]; then
    echo "Keeping the existing PalWorldSettings.ini (the Startup tab's values are written into it at every start)"
else
    echo "Creating PalWorldSettings.ini from DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini"
    mkdir -p "${CFG_DIR}"
    cp /mnt/server/DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini "${CFG_DIR}/PalWorldSettings.ini" || exit 1
fi

cd /mnt/server
## the config parser (pelican-eggs/Palworld-Config-Parser-Tool), which writes the Startup tab's values into
## PalWorldSettings.ini before every start. Octail pins a release and checks its SHA-256 (the digest GitHub lists for
## the release asset, also in the release's checksum.txt); staff can pick another release with PARSER_VERSION and
## must then give its SHA-256 in PARSER_SHA256.
PINNED_VERSION=v1.0.24
PINNED_SHA256=0bd863d2136fee303e9b3475d4990f2f8c3fedbd3ff2e3576605c1716c88b03c
VERSION="${PARSER_VERSION:-${PINNED_VERSION}}"
SHA256=$(echo "${PARSER_SHA256:-}" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')
if ! echo "${VERSION}" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
    echo "PARSER_VERSION must be a release tag such as ${PINNED_VERSION}, not ${VERSION}."
    exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${SHA256}" ]; then
    if [ "${VERSION}" != "${PINNED_VERSION}" ]; then
        echo "The config parser ${VERSION} has no recorded SHA-256: set PARSER_SHA256 to the digest of its"
        echo "PalworldServerConfigParser-linux-amd64 asset (the release's checksum.txt lists it), or use ${PINNED_VERSION}."
        exit 1
    fi
    SHA256="${PINNED_SHA256}"
fi
if ! echo "${SHA256}" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'; then
    echo "PARSER_SHA256 must be 64 hex characters (a SHA-256)."
    exit 1
fi
echo "Downloading the config parser ${VERSION}"
curl -fsSL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 20 -o PalworldServerConfigParser.download "https://github.com/pelican-eggs/Palworld-Config-Parser-Tool/releases/download/${VERSION}/PalworldServerConfigParser-linux-amd64" || {
    rm -f PalworldServerConfigParser.download
    echo "The download of the config parser ${VERSION} failed."
    exit 1
}
GOT=$(sha256sum PalworldServerConfigParser.download | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
if [ "${GOT}" != "${SHA256}" ]; then
    rm -f PalworldServerConfigParser.download
    echo "SHA-256 mismatch for the config parser ${VERSION} (expected ${SHA256}, got ${GOT})."
    exit 1
fi
mv -f PalworldServerConfigParser.download PalworldServerConfigParser
chmod +x PalworldServerConfigParser
## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Auto update the server on start.

variables.name: Admin Password
variables.description:
If specified, players must provide this password (via the in-game chat or RCON) to gain access to
administrator commands on the server.

variables.name: Public IP
variables.description:
Set this to the server public ip address.
Only needed if the allocation is a local ip, else the allocate ip will be used automatically

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: If specified, players must provide this password to join the server.

variables.name: RCON Port
variables.description: Does not need to be allocated!

variables.name: Crossplay Platforms
variables.description:
Comma-separated list of platforms allowed to connect. Valid values: Steam, Xbox, PS5, Mac. Example:
Steam,Xbox,PS5,Mac

variables.name: REST API Port
variables.description: Set by Octail when the server is created (the port after the game port). Lets the Players tab list, kick, ban and unban over Palworld's REST API; the API itself is never reachable from outside the node.

variables.name: Config Parser Version
variables.description: The release of the config parser the install downloads from GitHub (Palworld-Config-Parser-Tool). Octail checked v1.0.24; another release needs its SHA-256 in Config Parser SHA-256. Reinstall after changing it.

variables.name: Config Parser SHA-256
variables.description: Empty: only the release Octail checked (v1.0.24) installs. For another release, the SHA-256 of its PalworldServerConfigParser-linux-amd64 asset (listed in the release's checksum.txt).
